lines: Reads two signals as the horizontal and vertical parts of a point and rotates that point about the origin, by a fixed angle, by a continuous spin, or by both, with offsets applied before and after
Sets the rotation angle, -180 to 180 degrees
Attenuates and inverts the rotation CV, and at the full setting 5V there turns the pair by a further 180 degrees
Sets the speed of a continuous rotation added to the angle, -3 to 3: in L mode up to 90 turns per second either way, and in H mode 261.63 turns per second at the centre, doubling per unit
Attenuates and inverts the velocity CV, which is added to the velocity knob before the total is clamped to -3 to 3
Switches the velocity between L, a flat scale reaching 90 turns per second, and H, a volt per octave scale giving 261.63 turns per second at the centre of the velocity knob
Adds -10V to 10V to the first input before the rotation
Adds -10V to 10V to the second input before the rotation
Adds -10V to 10V to the first output after the rotation
Adds -10V to 10V to the second output after the rotation
Turns the pair away from the angle knob, 180 degrees for 5V at the full CV amount
Adds to the rotation velocity, scaled by the velocity CV amount
The horizontal part of the pair, and the number of channels here sets the polyphony of both outputs
The vertical part of the pair, read at the channel count of the other input
The horizontal part of the rotated pair, the cosine of the angle times the first input plus its sine times the second
The vertical part of the rotated pair, the cosine of the angle times the second input minus its sine times the first
Note — bypassing the module passes the first input straight to the first output and the second to the second
Reads two signals as the horizontal and vertical parts of a point, shears that point in both axes and rotates it about the origin, with offsets before and after and a soft limit on each output
Sets the rotation angle, -180 to 180 degrees
Attenuates and inverts the rotation CV, and at the full setting 5V there turns the pair by a further 180 degrees
Mixes -3 to 3 times the vertical input into the horizontal one before the rotation, which shears the curve sideways, despite the hover text naming it Scale
Attenuates and inverts the horizontal shearing CV, which is added to the Shearx knob
Mixes -3 to 3 times the horizontal input into the vertical one before the rotation, which shears the curve up and down
Attenuates and inverts the vertical shearing CV, which is added to the Sheary knob
Adds -10V to 10V to the first input before the shearing and the rotation
Adds -10V to 10V to the second input before the shearing and the rotation
Adds -10V to 10V to the first output after the rotation, before the saturator
Adds -10V to 10V to the second output after the rotation, before the saturator
Turns the pair away from the angle knob, 180 degrees for 5V at the full CV amount
Adds to the horizontal shearing, scaled by the trimpot under the Shearx knob
Adds to the vertical shearing, scaled by the trimpot under the Sheary knob
The horizontal part of the pair, and the number of channels here sets the polyphony of both outputs
The vertical part of the pair, read at the channel count of the other input
The horizontal part of the sheared and rotated pair, held to -10V to 10V by a parabolic saturator that softens the peaks shearing adds
The vertical part of the sheared and rotated pair, held to -10V to 10V by a parabolic saturator that softens the peaks shearing adds
Note — bypassing the module passes the first input straight to the first output and the second to the second
Three first-in first-out queues written and read by triggers, each holding up to 128 values, so a run of voltages can be stored and played back in the order it arrived
A trigger above 1V stores the voltage at each of the three In jacks as one more entry, and is ignored once 128 entries are held
A trigger above 1V takes the oldest entry out of each queue and holds it at the Out jacks; on an empty queue nothing is read and no trigger is sent
Above 0V, every entry read out is written back onto the end of the queue, so the stored run repeats
A trigger above 1V empties all three queues
The voltage stored in its own queue each time a write trigger arrives, and returned at the matching Out jack
A 10V trigger 1ms long each time an entry is actually read out
Carries 10V while the queues are empty and 0V while they hold anything
The entry read out of its own queue, held until the next read trigger
Note — the figure printed on the panel counts the entries now held, out of a maximum of 128, and the lamp column shows the same count as a bar
An eight-state sequencer driven by a Markov chain: every clock draws the next state at random from the probabilities set for the current one, and the output carries that state's value and input
Steps the chain on by hand, drawing the next state exactly like a clock pulse
Scales the output, 0 to 1, after the state value and the state input have been summed
Smooths the move from one state's knob value to the next, 0 for an instant change and 0.999 for the slowest glide; the signals at the State inputs are not slewed
Sets the value carried by the output while that state is current, -10V to 10V, added to the signal at that state's input
Makes that state the next one, in place of the state drawn at random, until the next clock arrives
Sets the relative probability of the chain moving from one state to another; the eight probabilities for a state are divided by their sum, so equal settings make every destination equally likely
Sets every probability of moving into that state to 0.5, from all eight states at once
Sets every probability of moving into that state to zero, from all eight states at once, so nothing leads there
Sets every probability of leaving that state to 0.5, towards all eight states at once
Sets every probability of leaving that state to zero, towards all eight states at once
A rise to 1V or more moves the chain on: the state drawn last becomes current and the one after it is drawn
The signal carried by the output while that state is current, added to that state's knob value and faded in and out over about 2.5ms to stop a click
A rise to 1V or more makes that state the next one, in place of the state drawn at random
The current state's knob value plus the signal at its input, scaled by the gain and limited to -10V to 10V
Carries the number of the current state, 0V for the first up to 7V for the eighth
A 10V trigger 1ms long when that state becomes the current one
Note — the red lamp beside a state marks the current state and the blue lamp marks the state the next clock will move to
Note — the number of channels at the first State input sets the polyphony of the Out jack
Menu — when every probability out of the current state is zero, the chain either stays on that state or treats all eight states as equally likely
An oscillator that runs a phasor around a polygon and gives its horizontal and vertical coordinates as two waveforms, the harmonic content set by the number of sides and by teeth added to the corners
Sets the pitch in octaves, -3 to 3, with 0 giving C4 at 261.63Hz
Attenuates the FM input, which at the full setting shifts the frequency by 700Hz per volt, through zero
Sets the number of sides of the polygon, 2.1 to 20; low values give a rich harmonic spectrum and high ones converge on a cosine at X and a sine at Y
Grows teeth on the corners of the polygon, 0 to 1, adding harmonics and trimming the output level by up to half as it rises
Attenuates and inverts the N CV, which at the full setting moves the number of sides by one per volt
Attenuates and inverts the T CV, which at the full setting moves the teeth value across its whole range for 10V
Sets the pitch a volt per octave, added to the pitch knob and clamped to -4 to 4 volts, and its channel count sets the polyphony of both outputs
Shifts the frequency through zero by 700Hz per volt at the full FM amount
Moves the number of polygon sides, scaled by the trimpot under the N knob; one channel here is applied to every voice, and a polyphonic cable gives each voice its own value
Moves the teeth value, scaled by the trimpot under the T knob; one channel here is applied to every voice, and a polyphonic cable gives each voice its own value
The horizontal coordinate of the point running around the polygon, -10V to 10V, a cosine at high side counts
The vertical coordinate of the point running around the polygon, -10V to 10V, a sine at high side counts
Menu — N: Quantization step rounds the number of sides to the nearest 0.25, 0.33, 0.50 or 1.00, or leaves it free
A delay line read with third-order Lagrange interpolation, built for waveguide and Karplus-Strong voices, flanging and chorus, with a second output tapped part way along the line
Shortens the delay by 0 to 16 sample periods, which compensates for the one sample every patch cable in the feedback loop adds
Sets the delay to one cycle of a pitch, -4 to 4 volts around C4 at 261.63Hz, and appears while the menu is set to Pitch
Sets the delay directly, 0.1ms to 1 second, and appears while the menu is set to Time
Taps the delay line for the Pickup output, 0 at the point the signal enters the line and 1 at the point it leaves
Attenuates and inverts the pickup position CV, which at the full setting moves the tap across the whole line for 10V
Scales the signal at the FBack input, 0 to 0.999, before it is added to the delay input
Switches the feedback between being added to the input and being subtracted from it, and lights the lamp for the sign in force
Sets the delay: read a volt per octave around C4 in Pitch mode, and in Time mode every volt lengthens the delay by a fifth of the knob setting
Moves the pickup tap along the delay line, scaled by the trimpot under the Pk Pos knob
The signal fed into the delay line
The signal returned into the delay line, scaled by the feedback trimpot and given the sign of the plus-minus button; nothing is routed back inside the module, so a cable is needed
The signal tapped part way along the delay line, at the point set by Pk Pos
The delayed signal, interpolated between samples so the delay can be a fraction of one, and limited to -20V to 20V
Menu — Delay specification chooses whether the Delay knob is read as a pitch, one cycle long, or as a time in milliseconds
WDelay.notes: The Pitch and Time knobs are built at the same place on the panel and only one is visible at a time, chosen by the Delay specification menu item; both are described. The delay input is coloured as a pitch port because Pitch is the default mode and the jack is read a volt per octave there; in Time mode the same jack is a time CV.
